description: The effectful shell (gig_reality_verify.sh) recursively repeats the exact 'report-blind' anti-pattern this feature exists to eliminate for the gig core -- just one level up, for the judge itself. After spawning the fresh claude -p judge, the script extracts the JSON object from JUDGE_RAW and constructs a JudgementResult purely from that self-reported text (extract_json_obj + JudgementResult.from_dict), then appends it to audit-reality.jsonl and conditionally writes the selfheal-request file -- with ZERO deterministic cross-check that the judge actually produced any trajectory/screenshot evidence during this run (e.g. no check that a new row was appended to ~/gig/trajectory/*/trajectory.jsonl with a timestamp inside [spawn_ts, spawn_ts+TIMEOUT_SECS], no check of PNG file mtimes). A judge that hallucinates 'verdict: true, reasoning: <plausible fabricated detail>' without ever touching :9222 would produce output structurally indistinguishable, to this script, from a judge that genuinely navigated and read the DOM. This is an accepted, common limitation of LLM-judge architectures (judge.py itself has the same property) so I am not marking it blocking on its own, but it directly undercuts the feature's stated purpose ('own-eyes... never trusting the core's self-report', behavioral-spec.md Purpose section) since the auditor's trust in the verifier is, itself, ultimately just as report-blind as the original problem this feature was built to fix.

evidence.snippet:
d = extract_json_obj(raw)
jr = gig_judge.JudgementResult.from_dict(d)
row = {"ts": int(time.time()), "verdict": jr.verdict, "reasoning": jr.reasoning, ...}
# no correlation against ~/gig/trajectory/*/trajectory.jsonl mtimes anywhere in this file

recommendation: Before accepting verdict:true, deterministically check that at least one trajectory row was appended under ~/gig/trajectory/ with mtime inside the spawn window; if none exists, downgrade to verdict:false/failure_reason:'no_trajectory_evidence' regardless of what the judge's JSON says.
